names.details: Fusṭāṭ: It is a well-known city in the land of Egypt, built by ‘Amr bin ‘Āṣ, the trusted vizier of Mu‘āviye. When Ḥażret-i ‘Ömer, may God be pleased with him, ruled, and the province of Egypt was conquered, the palace of the Tubba‘ (Himyarite kings) was found at the site of Fusṭāṭ. Later, Fusṭāṭ was developed and made prosperous. From the time of the kings of Egypt until the reign of Melik Aḥmed bin Ṭolun (Ahmad ibn Tulun), the capital of Egypt was located in this town. [translation]

title: Babylon/al-Fusṭāṭ/Old Cairo
details: The Barrington Atlas Directory notes: Fostat, Cairo
description: An ancient fortified city of the Nile Delta of Egypt, located at Babylon in the area today known as Coptic Cairo. Under the name al-Fusṭāṭ, it became the political center of Egypt following the Arab conquest in the 7th century CE.
